newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ALUMINUM - Argentine Aluar expansion talks drag on.
newsitem.headline: ALUMINUM - Argentine Aluar expansion talks drag on.

text.p: Aluminum refiner Aluminio Argentino (Aluar) said it is in final talks to hammer out gas contracts to power a possible $280 million expansion to boost output by 47 percent, a top official said.
"I presume that there will be news on this by the end of this month or at the beginning of October," said Aluar's administration manager Gregorio Krauchik.
But Aluar has been bogged down in talks over gas supplies for the expansion of the plant in Argentina's far southern region of Patagonia for almost a year.
Aluar would need to build a new 120 MW power plant if it goes ahead with the project. A main issue in present talks is the price of the gas to supply the new capacity.
Aluar already has its own 120-MW power station, and bought the 448-MW Futaleufu hydroelectric dam last year.
Asked whether the expansion could be put at risk by the recent plunge in aluminum prices to two-year lows, Krauchik said, "The project is not based on short-term considerations."
If Aluar decides to expand, it will spend $280-300 million boosting production to 250,000 tonnes a year from current output of 180,000 tonnes.
Basic and detailed engineering would have to be completed before construction could start, but Aluar hopes to finish installing the new facilities by 1999.
The estimated construction time of the expansion would be 30-36 months, according to Krauchik.

Among decisions still to be taken is whether Aluar will buy extra alumina to supply its expansion from present sole supplier Aluminum Company of America (Alcoa), Krauchik said. Alcoa sends Aluar alumina from Australia and Brazil.
Aluar exports about two thirds of its current output, particularly to Japan and Chile, and all extra production from the expansion would be sent abroad.
The final mix of financing has still to be fixed, although it would include a mix of both bank and suppliers' credit, as well as Aluar's own capital, Krauchik said.
Aluar recently signed a contract with French firm Pechiney to provide the design for a new electrolysis plant for the expansion, but has not signed any other contracts since, Krauchik said.

The head of another Argentine metals firm, who did not want to be named, said that the delays in Aluar's decision had sown doubts in his mind about whether the expansion would go ahead, but that he had no definite information on it.
